title: Prebiotics, low sugar and botanicals are reshaping the beverage market
access_note: Public HTML via trafilatura_precision; completeness not manually certified.

paragraphs.text: From gut health to stress relief, today’s top beverage and food brands are leaning into ingredients that are recognizable and purpose-driven.

The low‑sugar and functional soda segment has surged, according to a recent Circana report. Categories featuring claims like prebiotic fiber, botanical blends, adaptogens, added vitamins and low-sugar formulations are outpacing traditional diet sodas by double-digit annual growth. Consumers, especially Millennials and Gen Z, are actively trading traditional sweetened sodas for perceived wellness options – a key driver for this trend.
Legacy players & acquisition momentum
Legacy soda brands are accelerating into the better‑for‑you space:
- In May 2025, PepsiCo acquired Poppi for $1.95 billion to amplify its presence in functional beverages.
- In February 2025, Coca‑Cola launched “Simply Prebiotic,” offering 6g fiber, real juice, vitamins and zero added sugar.
- Startups, like Olipop, recently valued at $1.85 billion, are driving innovation around multi‑functional blends and fiber complexity.

More mergers, acquisitions and strategic partnerships are expected as major multinationals look to plug into functional portfolio growth – either by acquisition, co‑development or licensed collaborations, according to Circana.
4 trending ingredients
As consumers become more proactive about their health, the spotlight has turned to natural and functional ingredients – those that go beyond basic nutrition to support well-being in meaningful ways.

The functional food and drink movement is evolving quickly, with prebiotics, botanicals, real fruit juice and next-gen fibers taking center stage, according to Circana. Here’s a look at how key players are incorporating these trending ingredients to meet growing demand for wellness from the inside out:
- Prebiotics: inulin, chicory root, agave fiber – Poppi, Olipop and Coca-Cola’s upcoming offerings anchor on prebiotics for digestive wellness.
- Botanicals & adaptogens: hibiscus, ginseng, L‑theanine, ashwagandha, elderberry – touted for mood, stress or immunity benefits (per “functional food” trend analysis) .
- Real fruit juice/vitamins: Coca‑Cola’s Simply Prebiotic contains 25-30% juice plus vitamin C, potassium, iron and zinc alongside 6 grams of prebiotic fiber.
- Fiber blends beyond inulin: Next-gen fibers (like arabinoxylans) that promise more gut efficacy at lower doses, addressing stability and digestive tolerance.
Regulatory and legal risks: Lessons from Poppi
Poppi’s class action lawsuit (ending in an $8.9 million settlement in May 2025) over health claims around prebiotic labeling highlights critical regulatory landmines:
- FTC mandates: Structure/function claims must be honest and substantiated; misleading marketing can invite class‑action lawsuits.
- Risk areas include: Fiber dosage, sugar trade-offs, side effects, whole‑food messaging and disease claims.
6 critical focus areas for brand success and compliance
Brands must keep a close eye on several key focus areas to remain competitive and compliant in today’s market:
- Claims substantiation is essential and should be supported by clinical dosages and peer-reviewed research.
- In terms of label transparency, brands should clearly display gram-level information on fiber and sugar, including trade-offs related to timing.
- Ingredient innovation is another priority, with an emphasis on using next-generation fibers like arabinoxylan and incorporating stable botanicals.
- Regulatory oversight requires alignment with FTC, FDA and state advertising laws to ensure legal compliance.
- To build and maintain consumer trust, companies must provide full disclosure regarding potential side effects and product limitations.
- For strategic growth, exploring mergers and acquisitions can offer opportunities to scale rapidly and effectively.

title: Fresh Fizz brings clean label soda back to basics
access_note: Public HTML via trafilatura_precision; completeness not manually certified.

paragraphs.text: In a beverage aisle crowded with functional claims, Fresh Fizz is taking a different approach: simplicity. Founded by Rebecca and Yoni Schwartz, the New York–based soda company is built on a back-to-basics formula that uses herbs, spices, juices and natural sweeteners like honey, maple syrup and date syrup.

Fresh Fizz’s clean-label ethos informs every part of the business, from packaging to production to retail strategy, according to the founders. The brand calls out its ingredients directly on the front of the can — similar to RXBar’s approach — making it clear to consumers that what they see is what they get," says Rebecca Schwartz.
Production and sourcing

Formulating sodas without flavor extracts requires a different playbook. The team sources bulk frozen herbs and spices, steeps them into large-batch teas and then filters them down before adding juices and sweeteners. Most of the ingredients are sourced in the US but organic honey, which Yoni claims is nearly impossible to produce domestically, comes from South America.
Self-manufacturing has been a game-changer, Yoni adds, allowing Fresh Fizz to run production daily, maintain tighter quality control and launch new SKUs quickly.

The move to self-manufacturing was informed by early growing pains: an improperly filtered batch that nearly triggered a recall, Rebecca says. Instead of relying on co-packers, the founders opted to bring production in-house for more control and faster responsiveness. “It gives us flexibility,” Rebecca explains. “We don’t have to wait months for a production slot, and we can fill orders or test new flavors much faster.”
Retail and distribution: From neighborhood stores to national chains

Like many early-stage beverage brands, Fresh Fizz began with a boots-on-the-ground approach. Rebecca personally sold into neighborhood shops before gaining traction with local chains and eventually landing distribution through KeHE.

Today, Fresh Fizz has a presence across the Northeast and select regions in Southern California, with placements in natural and organic retailers such as MOM’s Organic and Fairway. Independent and health-conscious retailers remain the brand’s strongest channel, reflecting its consumer base of educated, label-savvy shoppers, Rebecca adds.

Sampling also is critical to Fresh Fizz’s retail success. Buyers and consumers alike can taste the difference in Fresh Fizz’s ingredient-first formulations, according to the founders. “When people try it, they immediately recognize the flavors as real and familiar,” says Rebecca.
Trends and category outlook: Beyond ‘functional’

The functional soda wave shows no sign of slowing, but Fresh Fizz is deliberately stepping outside of that trend. Instead of leaning into probiotics or adaptogens, the brand relies on the natural benefits of its ingredients without making overt claims. Ginger, hibiscus, tart cherry and mint are recognizable to consumers and appreciated for their inherent health properties, Rebecca notes.
Yoni adds that even major players are shifting. Poppi has downplayed its prebiotic messaging, while Spindrift has launched sodas with juice and water.
“Consumers are starting to come back to real food ingredients and more wholesome sweeteners,” Rebecca says.
Funding and growth: Scrappy, sustainable and slow

Unlike some fast-scaling competitors, Fresh Fizz has opted for a slower, more measured growth path. Funded through friends, family and personal savings, the brand has pieced together secondhand equipment through auctions and gradual upgrades. Yoni, who oversees production, has built much of the manufacturing setup himself.

“We’d rather grow slowly and in a more organic way than overextend,” Rebecca explains. That philosophy has not only kept the company lean but also allowed it to adapt to challenges without sacrificing quality, she adds.
Advice for startups: Start small, stay persistent
Reflecting on Fresh Fizz’s journey, the founders offers advice for other beverage entrepreneurs:
- Start small. Mistakes are inevitable, and it’s better to make them on a local scale than in a national launch.
- Don’t give up after a ‘no.’ Category managers and retail buyers turn over frequently; rejection often means “no for now.”
- Be careful with incentives. Free product giveaways can be costly, and sometimes saying no is the smarter path. If the product is strong enough, buyers will come back.

paragraphs.text: Bev Tech Innovator Set to be A Category – Defining Brand With Its New Disruptive Format and Focus on Fresh

In the wake of Poppi’s massive success and the recent acquisition by PepsiCo, the beverage industry is on high alert for the next functional soda disruptor— and it may have just arrived. Meet SIF, a Bev-Tech innovator redefining the way consumers experience carbonation, wellness, and on-the-go convenience, through one simple push of a button SIF is the pioneer in “fresh” modern soda via its personalized drink system and multi-use bottle.

SIF is the world’s first portable soda system, a capsule-and-bottle format that delivers fresh, customized, functional sodas with a simple push of a button — anytime, anywhere. The SIF drink system creates a delicious, cold, better-for-you soda that serves all your hydration needs while reducing waste and being so much better for our planet. With the $62 Billion functional beverage market in the US rapidly expanding and consumer demand for better-for-you, sustainable options at an all-time high, SIF is positioned to be the next category-defining brand.

The brainchild of a group of innovative founders and business leaders who are passionate about the modern soda category and also stewards of the environment, SIF has come to life as the new entrant into the category that provides consumers with drinks that furnish wellness, personalization, convenience and sustainability. “Modern soda is evolving rapidly from niche to necessity”, said Ron Navon, CEO and Founder SIF, “Our inspiration for SIF was the charm and nostalgia for historic siphon bottles with Nespresso/Keurig’s successful modern capsule approach and a true desire to create a better world one sip at a time. We are excited to enter into the category with a new and innovative format and are confident that alongside the RTD brands that we will help bolster the entire modern soda space and push its growth and penetration to new levels and audiences.”

With Zillennial consumers leading the charge, SIF is currently a DTC-first company, with future plans to scale into major mass consumer retailers like Whole Foods, Target, and Amazon. “Early research indicates that 74% of consumers tested would incorporate SIF into their daily routines” commented Ty Tonander, Chief Product Officer and Co-Founder, SIF. “And of those consumers, 91% expressed interest in participating in a subscription-based model. This strongly validates the potential for recurring revenue and robust financial performance.”

We agree with PepsiCo CEO Raymon Laguarta and his insight regarding new generations of consumers and how they behave. “New generations think about beverages in a different way. They prefer to have their own bottles and create their own drinks.”

Via its pre-launch activities, SIF is currently building a community of “SIF-ties” who can pre-order their SIF drink system on our waiting list. The product will be available in a pilot in South Florida in the coming year.
Now raising $500K to finalize prototyping and conduct a product market fit test. Investors looking for the next billion-dollar beverage play—this might just be it.
With a multiplier of 88x – early stage investors in Poppi who invested $25K earned a return of over $2 million!
Is SIF the next Poppi? Or think bigger – maybe the iPhone of the beverage category? Stay tuned.

title: Cove Soda Closes $15M Round to Fuel Innovation, Hiring
access_note: Public HTML via trafilatura_precision; completeness not manually certified.

paragraphs.text: Canadian beverage maker Cove Soda has closed on $15 million in new funding as it seeks to further fuel U.S. expansion.

The round was led by growth equity fund Vanterra Ventures, a division of New York-based firm Vanterra Capital, which has backed a variety of consumer health brands including Hu, Actual Veggies, Overnight Oats and Daily Harvest.

According to a press release, the round was also backed by a broad span of individual investors, notably Simple Food Ventures and GHOST co-founder Dan Lourenco. Other first-time and returning investors from pro sports and entertainment – The Palm Tree Crew, Diplo, Kygo, The Chainsmokers, Michael Rubin, Jack Eichel, Aaron Ekblad, Miles Teller, Matt Chapman, and JD Martinez – were involved as well.

The new capital will support the introduction of new flavors – Cove has “five or six” new-to-the-category innovations in the pipeline, CEO John MacLellan told us in September – as well as “hiring of key talent.”

Launched in 2016 by brothers John and Ryan MacLellan, Cove Soda has accelerated growth since pivoting focus from kombucha to prebiotic soft drinks in 2023. The Halifax, Nova Scotia-based beverage maker entered the U.S. in 2024, and can be found in over 7,000 retail doors including Sprouts, Whole Foods, Costco and Target. In September, Cove signed a distribution agreement with Keurig Dr Pepper (KDP) Canada to service accounts in the country.
Ellis Fried, Principal at Vanterra Ventures, has joined Cove’s Board of Directors.

“Cove is emblematic of that strategy as it brings the world’s first zero-sugar functional soda to market with delicious, nostalgic flavors, quickly winning over consumers across North America,” Fried said in a statement.

Cove is one of a host of prebiotic CSDs – alongside products from Evolution Fresh, Sparkling Ice, Bloom (Nutrabolt), Coca-Cola, Health-Ade, Suja (Slice) and others – seeking to seize momentum behind the category as created by breakout brands Olipop and Poppi.

paragraphs.text: San Diego, CA — Spade, the innovative healthy soda brand, is thrilled to announce it has exclusively been named the Official Soda of Power Slap for 2025. Founded by Dana White, in partnership with the UFC, Power Slap has rapidly gained a global fanbase, boasting over 20 million followers across platforms like Rumble, YouTube, Instagram & TikTok. Known for its electrifying matches and events, and incredibly viral content, this collaboration positions Spade at the center of this burgeoning movement.

As part of the agreement, Spade’s logo will be prominently displayed on the competition stage mat, on the leg of the iconic center podium, and featured across Power Slap’s social media content, reaching a massive and highly engaged audience.

“This is an excellent opportunity for Spade to reach millions of engaged viewers,” said Jake Berman, CMO of Spade. “We are thrilled to align with Power Slap and its dynamic growth. Spade is redefining soda with its all-natural, zero sugar sodas that prioritize health and taste in every sip. Crafted to deliver the full flavor of traditional sodas without the sugar or artificial ingredients, Spade features just six clean ingredients. Spade’s innovative formula not only satisfies soda cravings but also supports active lifestyles by providing a functional benefit with its added electrolytes, perfect for hydration and recovery. As a premium soda brand, Spade’s innovative and approachable branding resonates with the next-generation soda consumer while maintaining broad appeal, making it the go-to choice for those seeking a better, healthier soda experience. Beyond health, Spade is committed to sustainability, partnering with CleanHub to actively combat plastic waste and prevent pollution in our oceans. We’re not sure what their position is on getting caught in the rain, but Vita Coco definitely likes Piña Coladas, given it’s the latest flavor for their line of Coconut Juices with Pulp. Wyld

Cannabis-infused beverage maker Wyld has unveiled a new collection of D9 beverages. The lineup includes seven flavors – Raspberry Lime (10mg THC), Blackberry Lemon (10mg THC), Strawberry Guava (10mg THC, 10mg CBD), Watermelon (10mg THC, 10mg CBD), Mango (10mg THC, 10mg CBD), Clementine (2mg THC, 20mg CBD) and White Peach (2mg THC, 20mg THC). For more information, visit wyldcbd.com.
Free AF

Free AF has expanded its portfolio of non-alcoholic canned cocktails with three new offerings: Margarita, Chili Margarita and Mango Margarita. The products are now available at Sprouts Farmers Market and Target. For more information, visit us.af-drinks.com.
Sēkwl Beverage House

Sēkwl has launched a line of adaptogenic sparkling waters made with functional mushrooms, sold in six flavors including Hibiscus, Grapefruit, Lemon Ginger, Chamomile, Blue Spruce and Cacao. Consumers can purchase the sparkling waters on the brand’s website for $48 per 12-pack of 12 oz. cans and $96 per 24-pack of 12 oz. cans. For more information, visit drinksekwl.com.
Joyburst

Ahead of the film’s release, Joyburst is promoting Lilo & Stitch (the 2025 live-action version) with a new Tropical Fruit Punch flavor. According to the brand, the new flavor “captures the spirit of ohana – family, connection and joy.” Additionally, the brand has entered the powdered hydration space with the release of Hydration Stick Packs in Strawberry-Lemonade and Watermelon Varieties. For more information, visit joyburst.com.
Raw Generation

Each set includes juices crafted with 40 raw fruits and vegetables. Each pack contains seven rainbow sippers (red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple and pink). Little Sippers are available on Raw Generation’s website for $99.99 per 28-pack (four weeks’ worth of cold-pressed juices). For more information, visit rawgeneration.com/products/sippers.
Melo

Kava-based beverage brand Melo has introduced a Tahitian Lime flavor to its lineup of canned relaxation drinks, alongside an updated sleek can design. The launch comes after a fire at Melo’s co-packer last month wiped out the brand’s entire finished inventory, according to co-founder and CEO Amy Bett. The addition of Tahitian Lime rounds out the brand’s zero-sugar, zero-calorie lineup, which includes Passionfruit Orange Guava and Banana Cream flavors. The updated cans will roll out on the brand’s website, with retail expansion continuing across more than 250 stores later this month. For more information, visit drinkmelo.co.
C4

Each serving also has 8 grams of the patented VELOX blend of L-Arginine and L-Citrulline and 8 grams of CarnoSyn Beta-Alanine. C4 Alpha Bomb will be available for $54.99 beginning May 10. For more information, visit cellucor.com/pages/c4-energy.

For more information, visit kraftheinz.com/en-CA/kool-aid/products.

For more information, visit drinkhint.com.

Sparkling non-alcoholic beverage maker TÖST has unveiled its latest creation: Sangria. The new beverage introduces blood orange and red grape to the brand’s signature blend of white tea, berries and botanicals. TÖST Sangria is available at select retailers nationwide and on the brand’s website for $27 per 3-pack of 750ml bottles. For more information, visit tostbeverages.com.

paragraphs.text: BevNET’s annual “Best Of” Awards celebrate the people, brands, products, and ideas that are shaping the future of the beverage industry. Since 2007, these honors have recognized innovation, influence, and excellence, and helped shine a spotlight on both breakout stars and established category leaders.
As 2025 enters its final stretch, BevNET is calling for nominations for the BevNET Best Of 2025 Awards, which will be presented live on stage at BevNET Live on December 8 in Marina del Rey, CA.
The deadline to submit nominations is Friday, October 31, 2025.
What Makes These Awards Special

With nearly two decades of history, the Best Of Awards represent one of the most meaningful recognitions in the beverage space. They acknowledge progress across categories — from functional innovation and brand building to packaging and marketing.
This year’s awards are presented by Zuckerman Honickman, a proud supporter of beverage entrepreneurs and industry trailblazers.
Categories Open for Nominations:
- Brand of the Year
- Person of the Year
- Rising Stars
- Best New Products
- Best Packaging Design
- Best Marketing Campaign

There is no limit to the number of nominations you may submit, and each entry may be considered across multiple categories. Brands are welcome to nominate themselves. Agencies submitting on behalf of clients must fill out a separate form for each company.
All nominations will be reviewed and published on BevNET.com after the submission deadline. Winners will be announced during the live awards ceremony on December 8, 2025, at BevNET Live L.A..
For those in the beverage space, this is an opportunity to highlight the work that’s left an impression in 2025.
Looking Back to Look Ahead
Our 2024 honorees reflect the diversity and innovation happening across categories:
- Brands of the Year: Olipop and Poppi redefined functional soda and drove mass consumer adoption.
- Person of the Year: David Crooch, co-founder of Ritual Beverage Co., led the charge in premium non-alcoholic spirits.
- Rising Stars: Just Ice Tea, Recess, and barcode each brought bold vision to wellness, functionality, and brand expression.
From household names to emerging challengers, these winners demonstrated how innovation, storytelling, and execution is shaping what’s next in beverage.

title: Crystal Light launches book-inspired limited-edition beverage flavours

paragraphs.text: Crystal Light is tapping into the booming #BookTok trend with the launch of three limited-edition drink flavours inspired by popular literary genres.
The new range includes Hibiscus Lemonade, Prickly Pear Lemonade and Passion Fruit, with each flavour designed to pair with a different reading experience – romance, mystery and fantasy, respectively.

The launch comes as book clubs and reading-focused social media content continue to surge in popularity. According to the brand, #BookTok has now generated more than 370 billion views globally, creating new opportunities for food and beverage brands to connect with lifestyle-driven consumer trends.

Crystal Light said the range was created to “refresh the reading ritual” by combining flavour innovation with functional hydration. All three products are marketed as zero-sugar beverages aimed at consumers seeking lighter refreshment options.

The company described Hibiscus Lemonade as delivering a “light and sweet” flavour profile inspired by romance novels, while Prickly Pear Lemonade offers a more “unexpected twist” aligned with mystery themes. Passion Fruit, meanwhile, was developed to reflect the bold and immersive nature of fantasy storytelling.
To support the launch, Crystal Light has partnered with author and influencer Brooke Averick, whose debut novel, Phoebe Berman’s Gonna Lose It, is scheduled for release in May.

The collaboration reflects a growing trend of beverage and snack brands aligning with online reading communities and creator-led marketing to engage younger consumers through culturally relevant experiences.

Crystal Light said the flavours are designed for occasions ranging from book clubs to personal wellness and self-care routines, positioning the drinks as part of a broader lifestyle experience rather than solely a refreshment product.
The limited-edition range is available nationwide across US retailers while supplies last.

title: Gen Z trends, UPF debate & Coca-Cola’s beverage pivot
access_note: Public HTML via trafilatura_precision; completeness not manually certified.

paragraphs.text: From Gen Z’s wellness-driven eating habits to the policy challenges over ultra-processed foods – and Coca-Cola’s beverage focus – this week highlights how health and reformulation are reshaping the grocery aisle

As younger consumers reshape what “healthy” means, policymakers wrestle with how to regulate processed foods and major beverage brands like The Coca-Cola Co. pivot toward protein and low sugar, the industry continues navigating an era of health-driven innovation.
Young consumers redefine food & nutrition

According to new data from SPINS, Gen Z and Millennial consumers are driving what the data analyst firm calls a “nutrient-density renaissance.” These shoppers prioritize protein, fiber and gut health, seek bold global flavors and clean labels. More than half say they follow a high-protein diet, and nearly 90% say they avoid ingredients such as high-fructose corn syrup or artificial sweeteners.

Generational research by Circana also shows younger consumers favor convenience, flexibility and digital-first shopping, seeking energy, productivity and work-life balance – while older consumers lean toward preventative care and simplicity.
Pending ultra-processed food regulation creates a challenging terrain

Experts warn that any blanket regulation of ultra-processed foods could backfire – particularly if paired with reduced public health investment – because current classification systems (like NOVA) may group dissimilar foods together and penalize convenient fortified options.

In the debate over regulating UPFs, a survey by the Non‑GMO Project found that while 72% of US consumers say they are trying to avoid UPFs, many don’t actually know how to define them – and most significantly underestimate how much they consume. Trust in food companies is low too: 47% reported little or no trust.

Meanwhile, in California, a landmark law signed by Gov. Gavin Newsom will require the state to define “ultra-processed foods of concern” by mid-2028, begin phasing them out of school meals by 2029, and fully ban vendors from supplying them by 2032/35.
Big beverages lean into protein & sugar reduction

The Coca‑Cola Company is responding to shifts in consumer habits – including those driven by appetite-suppression drugs like GLP-1s – by doubling down on zero/low sugar offerings and targeting the protein-rich segment.

As sugar awareness is getting stronger among younger consumers, and taste/texture demands are rising, Coca-Cola is expanding production of ultra-filtered milk, ready-to-drink protein shakes and otherwise positioning itself to meet a more health-conscious, convenience-seeking market.

title: Spadel Invests in Living Things, a Leading Player in the Booming Gut-Health Soda Category
access_note: Public HTML via trafilatura_precision; completeness not manually certified.

paragraphs.text: The Source Ventures, Spadel Group’s venture capital fund, has participated in the latest investment round of Living Things, a fast-growing UK beverage company leading the emerging category of gut-health sodas. This investment supports The Source Ventures’ ambition to partner with visionary European entrepreneurs who are disrupting the beverage industry with healthy, natural and sustainable products.

Launched just over two years ago, Living Things has rapidly established itself as one of the most dynamic players in the fast-growing “gut-health soda” segment. Developed and produced in the United Kingdom, their lightly sparkling drinks are low in sugar, high in fibre and enriched with prebiotics and probiotics, delivering billions of live cultures per can. Living Things’ beverages also contain no added sugar or sweeteners and deliver fewer than 13 kcal per 100 ml. The brand is also committed to environmental sustainability, with fully recyclable cans.

For this innovative young brand, a focus on health and sustainability doesn’t come at the expense of taste, with their drinks coming in five refreshing flavours: Raspberry & Pomegranate, Peach & Blood Orange, Lemon & Ginger, Watermelon & Lime, and Rhubarb & Apple.

“Tasting good and doing good don’t have to be in conflict”, says Living Things founder Jonathan Relph, who, alongside co-founder Ben Vear, started Living Things just over two years ago. “Today’s consumers want soft drinks that taste great, offer real health benefits and that are environmentally conscious. With Living Things, we’ve created a new class of soda that does all three.”
And this clearly resonates with consumers.

Since its launch, Living Things has experienced significant growth, with distribution approaching 25,000 points of availability, including leading British retailers like Tesco, Waitrose, Ocado, Boots and others, as well as a rapidly growing number of cafés, delis and other foodservice locations and retailers across European markets including Ireland, the Netherlands, Belgium, Switzerland and the Czech Republic. The brand is particularly successful with the fast-growing, health-conscious consumer seeking alternatives to traditional diet sodas, alcohol and artificial ingredients.

After significant growth in the US, the gut-health category is now expanding in Europe. This trend is of course not only about Living Things: the gut-health soda category is booming globally, with explosive growth in the US these last years. As awareness about fibre intake and gut health continues to rise across Europe, the category is entering a new phase of expansion.

“Living Things is positioned at the forefront of this shift”, comments Clément Yvorra, Global Business Development Manager at Spadel and Head of The Source Ventures. “The company plays within the broader better-for-you soda movement, bringing flavours, natural ingredients and a lifestyle-driven brand identity that resonates with young, bold and socially conscious consumers.”
Living Things is now preparing its next phase of growth.

The new fundraising round, which includes The Source Ventures investing pari passu alongside other top-tier drinks investors, including former Coca Cola Marketing Director Kris Robbens and Fulfil Nutrition Founder Barry Connolly, will support international expansion, investments in marketing, team growth and operational scaling, with a medium-term ambition to become a €100m+ brand in the European soda landscape.

“We’re delighted to support Living Things’ ambition to become a leading player in the fast-growing gut-health soda segment. The brand perfectly embodies the values we believe will shape the future of the beverage industry: naturality, functionality, sustainability and great taste,” says Clément Yvorra.

About Spadel: Spadel is a European and family-owned group with a mission to offer consumers, throughout their lives, natural responses to their hydration and refreshment needs. It markets brands of natural mineral water, spring water and refreshing drinks based on natural mineral water: Spa and Bru in the Benelux, Devin in Bulgaria, Wattwiller and Carola in France. It also sells natural and less sweetened energy drinks under the Zyla brand. Sustainable development is naturally part of the DNA of the Spadel Group. In 2024, the Spadel Group generated a turnover of 379.3 million euros. At the end of 2024, the group employed 1,359 people. Spadel and all of its brands are B Corp certified.

title: The new beverage battleground is in AI recommendations vs. shelf space
access_note: Public HTML via trafilatura_precision; completeness not manually certified.

paragraphs.text: In the exponentially expanding world of generative engine optimization, brands that position themselves as a solution to consumers’ needs are the ones that will increasingly show up in AI recommendations.

Within the beverage category, functional beverages continuously showed up as the top recommendation in AI answers, regardless of whether the product moves volumes or is cheaper, according to recent research from 5WPR AI Communications.

The AI communications firm looked across 60 prompts in ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity and Google AI for its 5W AI Visibility Index report and found that functional beverages surfaced more than brands positioned around flavor, taste or sales volume.
AI prompts from users are function-focused, according to Ronn Torossian, founder of 5WPR AI Communications.

Within energy drinks, AI recommendations consistently favored Celsius, Liquid Death, Olipop and Poppi, whereas category giants Red Bull and Monster, which have moved significant unit sales over the last several decades, ranked lower.

“What surprised me most was how completely uncorrelated sales and citation share turned out to be,” Torossian said. “Red Bull and Monster have owned the energy category for 20 years by unit sales. They’re the brands everyone thinks of first at the store, yet they’re sitting at second and seventh place in how often AI names them.”
Why?
AI rewards the brands that answer a question

With health as the main theme across consumer AI beverage prompts, AI agents are scraping the digital landscape and pulling up brands that tell a clear benefit narrative around their product, along with updated earned media and independent coverage, according to Torossian.

Traditionally brands relied on search engine optimization (SEO) to show higher in search engine rankings. Now, brands are competing in GEO to show up as the first answers in AI searches. Ultimately, a brand’s relevance, or citation share, in an AI recommendation is increasingly based on two factors: what a consumer is searching for and how a brand answers those questions across their media presence.

“Nobody asks a chatbot for the best-selling energy drink,” Torossian said. “They ask for the healthy one, the gut-healthy one, the clean one, the one with electrolytes. The brand that has clearly and repeatedly answered that specific question in the public record is the brand that gets named back.”
In Celsius’ case, the brand expanded its citation share into the female and fitness energy drink space when it acquired Alani Nu in February 2025.
“The Alani Nu acquisition matters more than people realize,” Torossian said. “It’s not just added revenue. It’s added citation surface.”

Another example is PepsiCo’s Poppi acquisition last year, where the CPG giant is playing in the prebiotic soda space – a category Poppi and Olipop created, Torossian says. Both Poppi and Olipop consistently show up as leading gut-health soda recommendations in AI search, according to 5WPR.

When it comes to AI, market leadership is not enough. Consumers are not searching for the best-selling energy drink, Torossian argues. They are looking for the one that supports a specific need, whether that’s energy, hydration or gut health.

“Market leadership built through decades of distribution deals and shelf placement doesn’t automatically transfer into that answer,” he said. “It’s an entirely different kind of leadership that AI is rewarding.”
Flavor wins at the shelf but function wins in AI
For flavor-forward brands, they may win on retail shelves because consumers build a relationship with the product over time, Torossian argues, whereas citation is earned through a public record.
“Loyalty and citation are earned in two completely different places, through two completely different mechanisms,” he said. “Flavor wins at the shelf, through taste, habit and repeat purchase.”
By contrast, AI recommendations are built on documented information.

“AI doesn’t experience taste. It reads,” Torossian said. “A brand can have won over thousands of loyal repeat customers on flavor alone and still be functionally invisible to an AI engine, simply because nobody’s written down what the product does beyond ‘tastes good.’”
He emphasized the contrast: “The two forms of success just don’t overlap the way people assume they would.”
One flavor-forward brand, Spindrift, which focuses on natural flavors, is still picked up by AI, but largely as a clean-label and low-sugar sparkling water.
“Even Spindrift’s citation success is quietly borrowing a small functional claim to get in the door,” Torossian said.
The window is narrowing for flavor-first brands
For AI visibility, flavor has a shrinking shelf life, Torossian said.
“Flavor is what turns that first-time buyer into a repeat customer once they’ve actually tried it,” he said. “Function is what gets a startup discovered in the first place.”
While flavor-centric brands can still compete today, Torossian says functional positioning will become increasingly important as AI-driven discovery grows.

“As more competitors attach a real function to their brand story, the AI engines will have more well-documented functional options to choose from for every query,” he said. “The purely flavor-driven brands will simply get crowded out of the answer.”
Torrossian adds: “It’s not that flavor becomes worthless. It stays essential for retention. But as a standalone strategy for AI visibility, it has a shrinking shelf life.”
